sam (People Ops): Flagging an odd docs/tax issue for Andres. He shows up with both a 2026 1099-NEC and a W-2 for overlapping pay in Mar 2026 after a short Mexico remote stint. Can payroll confirm which payments were run as vendor vs payroll?

julia (Payroll): Yep saw this in the feed. March pay had two ledger lines: vendor payout (contractor invoice processed 2026-03-05) and then a Redwood payroll run on 2026-03-31 that included the same gross amount after conversion. System generated 1099 for vendor and W-2 for payroll. Need invoice copy + contract conversion date to decide correction path.

andres (Employee): I was in Mexico from 2026-03-10 -> 2026-04-20. Initially contracted through local vendor, then converted to employee effective 2026-03-25. I uploaded invoice, travel dates, boarding passes to HR:/onboard/andres/mexico-2026. I didn't expect double forms :grimacing:

natalie (Tax): Thanks Andres. Key issues: (1) IRS reporting duplication — we cannot have identical income on 1099 and W-2 for same taxpayer; (2) Mexican tax nexus — working 41 days likely doesn't trigger 183-day residency, but local payroll/reporting by the vendor matters. We need to either revoke/correct the 1099 or issue a W-2c depending on which was reported first to the IRS. Also check if US Social Security/Medicare was mistakenly withheld on vendor pay.

ravi (Finance): I pulled payments: vendor ACH to LocalVendor MX on 2026-03-05 ($4,200), payroll ACH to Andres on 2026-03-31 ($4,200 net after tax). The vendor payment coded CONTRACTOR_EXPENSE; payroll payment coded PAYROLL_GROSS. Bank remits: vendor remitted in MXN on 03-06, payroll remits to US tax vendor on 04-05. So both were likely reported. We need JE to reverse one side depending on decision.

julia (Payroll): If vendor 1099 has been e-filed, correcting a 1099 is possible via corrected 1099-NEC (box values set to corrected). But if W-2 already filed and deposited taxes, we may need W-2c to correct boxes. Natalie, which path do we prefer? Revoke 1099 or issue W-2c?

natalie (Tax): Preferred path: revoke the 1099 (file corrected 1099 showing zeroed amount) if the vendor payment was actually a misc coding duplicate and the economic employer is Redwood. Rationale: W-2 should reflect wages if the individual was an employee as of 03-25 and services post-conversion belong on payroll. But we must ensure Mexico vendor didn't legitimately pay wages for pre-conversion period. Action items: (A) confirm invoice dates and scope from Andres; (B) get vendor statement/contract showing the payment was pre-conversion; (C) get uploader proof that conversion date is 03-25. If vendor legitimately paid for work before 03-25 then we keep 1099 for that portion and only correct overlap.

manager-liz (Manager): I confirm Andres converted on 2026-03-25 per my approval email. He performed some days before conversion as contractor. I'm ok with correcting the 1099 for overlap days. Approve whatever docs Tax + Payroll need.

andres (Employee): Uploaded contractor invoice 2026-03-01 (services Mar 1-15) and conversion offer letter (signed 2026-03-24, effective 03-25). Looks like the vendor payment covered Mar 1-15 and payroll included full-month accidentally. Happy to accept correction that leaves vendor for Mar 1-15 and payroll for Mar 25-31.

julia (Payroll): Ok that helps. We'll do a split: vendor for Mar1-15 gross, payroll for Mar25-31 wages. Need to reverse duplicated Mar16-24 portion on one side. I will compute overlap amounts and propose adjustments. Also checking whether Social Security/Medicare was withheld incorrectly on the vendor line  it's not usually withheld for vendor payments.

ravi (Finance): Please send the overlap numbers and I'll create JE template for the reversal: JE-2026-411 ("Corr: Andres contractor/payroll overlap"). Also note potential FX differences since vendor remitted in MXN.

compliance-bot: Ticket CREATED: PAYROLL-INC-1769990001. Actions required: vendor statement, invoice, conversion letter, manager approval. https://payroll.redwood.com/cases/PAYROLL-INC-1769990001

julia (Payroll): Quick calc: vendor paid gross 4,200 MXN-equivalent for Mar1-15. Payroll recorded gross 4,200 USD for whole month and withheld taxes. Overlap estimated ~1,900 USD for Mar1-15 double-reported. I'll attach precise run totals and YTD.

natalie (Tax): Once Julia confirms amounts, we will: (1) file corrected 1099-NEC to zero overlap amount (send corrected 1099 to IRS/recipient), (2) update payroll ledger and, if needed, issue W-2c only if payroll reported wrong boxes. If IRS deposits already occurred, we'll coordinate with IRS to explain correction. Also will check with Mexican counsel whether vendor withholding matters for Mexican filing.

andres (Employee): Appreciate the plan. Will provide any statements vendor needs to cancel or reallocate payment if required. If there's an off-cycle to adjust net pay, happy with whichever minimizes delay.

manager-liz (Manager): Approve corrected 1099 approach. Please keep me cc'd on communications to Andres.

julia (Payroll): I'll produce the overlap worksheet + proposed JE by EOD and tag `payroll-1099-w2-overlap`.

ravi (Finance): JE ready once Julia posts numbers. I'll label JE-2026-411 and attach to case.

natalie (Tax): Noted. I'll prepare the corrected 1099 filing instructions and reach out to external counsel for MX specifics. Expect update in 3 business days.

julia (Payroll): Uploaded overlap calc and proposed run adjustments to finance drive. Link: https://payroll.redwood.com/docs/andres-overlap-1769990001. Off-cycle not needed if we correct vendor records and issue corrected 1099; payroll net will remain for post-conversion days.

compliance-bot: UPDATE: PAYROLL-INC-1769990001 assigned to julia (Payroll). Reminder: keep records for 7 years.

andres (Employee): Thanks team 64f0 will watch for docs. Appreciate the quick coordination.
